pairs.title: Immeuble, 1 rue Le Peletier, Paris 9e
pairs.shows: Full corner facade of an elaborate commercial/insurance building: a tall domed corner tourelle topped with an iron-crested finial, sculptural dormers, and a busy, varied roofline in place of a plain 45-degree attic — a strong example of the post-1884 discontinuity.
pairs.street: 1, rue Le Peletier, Paris 9e (architect Georges Morin-Goustiaux)

pairs.title: Castel Béranger, 14 rue La Fontaine
pairs.shows: Oblique full-facade view of Guimard's Castel Béranger: mixed brick/stone bays, sculptural iron balconies, and an irregular roofline with varied dormer forms.
pairs.street: 14, rue La Fontaine, Paris 16e (architect Hector Guimard)

pairs.title: Immeuble, 31 rue de Fleurus (album Ch. Girault)
pairs.shows: Full corner facade in raking light: a tall, steep mansard/comble roof carrying multiple distinct dormer forms (round-headed, segmental, gabled), tall chimneys, a weathervane, and iron-cresting on the balcony railings — a clean discontinuity-test image.
pairs.street: 31, rue de Fleurus, Paris 6e (architect Charles Girault; this print is filed within a Commons album titled "Immeuble avenue Henri Martin" but the photo itself is captioned 31 rue de Fleurus, Paris — the album appears to bundle several of Girault's works)

pairs.title: Castel Béranger, upward facade view
pairs.shows: Steep upward-angled view showing the roofline clearly: varied dormers, tall chimneys, and iron cresting along the parapet.
pairs.street: 14, rue La Fontaine, Paris 16e (architect Hector Guimard)

pairs.title: Castel Béranger entrance gate
pairs.shows: Detail of the whiplash wrought-iron entrance gate and carved stone surround — evidence of the enriched decorative vocabulary of the period, not the roofline itself.
pairs.street: 14, rue La Fontaine, Paris 16e (architect Hector Guimard)

pairs.title: Immeuble Lavirotte, 29 avenue Rapp
pairs.shows: Full frontal facade of Lavirotte's masterpiece: sculpted dormers and iron cresting at the roofline over an exuberant ceramic and stone facade — a textbook discontinuity-test image.
pairs.street: 29, avenue Rapp, Paris 7e (architect Jules Lavirotte; won the Ville de Paris facade competition)

pairs.title: 29 avenue Rapp, alternate view
pairs.shows: Alternate full-facade daylight view of the same building, confirming the roofline dormers and cresting from a different angle/lighting.

pairs.title: 29 avenue Rapp, roofline detail
pairs.shows: Close detail of the upper comble zone: sculpted dormers, cresting figures, and ceramic ornament at the parapet — direct close-up evidence of the elaborated roofline.

pairs.title: Immeuble Les Arums, 33 rue du Champ de Mars
pairs.shows: Full oblique facade with bow windows and dense floral art nouveau ornament in stone and iron; upper roofline partially visible at frame edge.
pairs.street: 33, rue du Champ de Mars, Paris 7e (architect Octave Raquin; won the 1902 Ville de Paris facade competition)

pairs.title: Immeuble, 130 rue Réaumur
pairs.shows: Corner building with a domed corner tourelle and an elaborate mansard/comble roofline carrying multiple dormers and iron-crested balcony railings. Construction date not given in the Commons record; rue Réaumur was cut through in 1897 and most of its buildings date circa 1898-1905, so this is stylistically consistent with the family but the exact year is left blank rather than guessed.

pairs.title: 1-3 Place Saint-Michel
pairs.shows: Grand corner Haussmannian building on a major place: tall arched shopfronts, wrought-iron balconies at 2nd and top floor, heavily dressed stone bays, steep zinc mansard with dormers -- the 'grand' end of the class range where bays/balconies/cornice are elaborated well beyond a modest building while the ground-floor arcade rhythm still reads as door-scaled openings.

pairs.title: 5-7 Place Saint-Michel
pairs.shows: Second grand corner building on the same place, giving a same-scale comparison pair: full mansard, iron balconies at two levels, arcaded ground floor with awnings -- confirms the grand-end proportions are a type, not a one-off.

pairs.title: 16 rue Etienne-Marcel
pairs.shows: Near-frontal full elevation of a comfortable-tier Haussmannian building: sculpted cartouche/cherub keystone over the entry, two tiers of wrought-iron balconies with carved consoles, pilastered bays -- a clear mid-point between plain modest housing and the palatial grand end, useful for showing door scale staying constant while balcony/window enrichment increases one notch.

pairs.title: 53 rue Blanche
pairs.shows: Excellent full-elevation frontal shot showing the family's core claim directly: a modestly sized arched double door at ground level, essentially unchanged in scale from a plainer building, below four upper floors of regularly repeated bays with wrought-iron balconies, foliate keystones and a dentillated cornice -- door stays small, everything above it grows more elaborate.

pairs.title: 31 rue Du Sommerard
pairs.shows: Frontal corner elevation, comfortable tier: pedimented window surrounds on the piano nobile, a balustraded balcony course, plain but generously sized door at grade -- again shows the door holding roughly constant scale while window dressing and balcony ironwork step up in richness going up the facade and up the class range.

pairs.title: Maison, Faubourg St Antoine 122 (vue prise en 1904)
pairs.shows: Small plain shopfront house on a faubourg street: narrow bays, unadorned window surrounds, shutters, ground-floor shops crowding a small door -- the plainest, most modest end of the range. NOTE: construction date (1730) predates the 19th-century Haussmann period targeted by this corpus; kept as the clearest legible frontal example of 'modest faubourg' massing found on Commons, flag for operator review.
pairs.street: 122 rue du Faubourg-Saint-Antoine, 12e arrondissement, Paris (photographed 1904; construction inscribed on mount as 1730, built by the hopital des enfants trouves and the famille d'Aligre)

pairs.title: Rue St Merri 17-19 (Juin 1913)
pairs.shows: Frontal shot of two narrow, plain apartment buildings on a medieval-pattern street: minimal window dressing, small iron balconettes only at a couple of floors, plain shopfronts and a small round-arched carriage door at grade -- a clean modest-tier reference with door legible and undecorated.
pairs.street: 17-19 rue St Merri, 4e arrondissement, Paris (photographed June 1913 by Henri Godefroy)

pairs.title: 2 boulevard Voltaire
pairs.shows: Clean frontal full-elevation shot of a standard, unexceptional Haussmannian building on an ordinary (not grand) boulevard: regular bays, modest balcony ironwork at two floors only, plain door under a red awning at grade, simple dentil cornice -- a useful mid-range anchor between the modest faubourg examples and the ornate comfortable/grand ones.

pairs.title: Hotel particulier, angle rue Legendre / rue Leon-Cosnard, Paris XVIIe
pairs.shows: Corner treatment on a freestanding hotel particulier: chamfered/angled corner bay in brick-and-stone banding, distinct roofline break (mansard hip turning the corner) and its own fenestration rhythm independent of the two adjoining street facades.
pairs.street: 19 rue Legendre / rue Leon-Cosnard, 17e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Hotel particulier style troubadour, 30 rue de Tocqueville, Paris XVIIe
pairs.shows: Full corner elevation of a freestanding mansion: the chamfered corner reads as its own short facade with a single bay of windows, balconies, and a dedicated mansard/dormer above, distinct in rhythm from the long facades either side.
pairs.street: 30 rue de Tocqueville, angle rue Legendre / rue Leon-Cosnard, 17e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Hotel particulier, angle rue Spontini / rue de Longchamp, Paris XVIe
pairs.shows: A restrained ashlar corner block of a hotel particulier: symmetrical three-bay corner with its own balconies and roofline, clearly a distinct short facade turning the angle between two streets.
pairs.street: angle rue Spontini / rue de Longchamp, 16e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Immeuble, angle boulevard de Port-Royal / rue Broca, Paris Ve
pairs.shows: Classic rounded-corner apartment block (rotonde): the curved bay carries its own vertical window/balcony rhythm and a distinct domed roof cap, clearly separate from the straight bays on each street front.
pairs.street: 46 boulevard de Port-Royal, angle rue Broca, 5e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Immeuble post-haussmannien, 27 boulevard Jules-Sandeau, Paris XVIe
pairs.shows: Bowed/rounded corner rotonde with sculpted keystones and its own balcony rail pattern, capped by a domed corner roof that breaks from the mansard lines of the adjoining wings.
pairs.street: 27 boulevard Jules-Sandeau, angle rue Eugene Labiche, 16e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Immeuble Guimard, angle rue Gros / rue de la Fontaine, Paris XVIe
pairs.shows: Art Nouveau treatment of a full-height rounded corner tower (Hector Guimard): the curved prow carries continuous stacked balconies and its own turret roof, entirely independent in rhythm from the two straight facades it joins.
pairs.street: 41 rue Gros, angle rue Agar, 16e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Immeubles, angle rue du Renard / rue Saint-Merri, Paris IVe (c.1895-1899)
pairs.shows: Archival photograph of an older corner building with a distinct narrow chamfered facade at the street junction, shop signage at ground floor, and a roofline/dormer treatment that reads as its own short facade rather than a repeated module.
pairs.street: angle rue du Renard / 18-20 rue Saint-Merri, 4e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Immeuble, angle rue Monsieur-le-Prince / boulevard Saint-Michel, Paris VIe
pairs.shows: Full-height rounded Haussmannian corner rotonde with its own dormer-ringed dome roof, continuous curved balconies, and ground-floor storefront wrapping the chamfer independently of the two straight wings.
pairs.street: 56 boulevard Saint-Michel, angle rue Monsieur-le-Prince, 6e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Old Bakery - 23 rue des Francs-Bourgeois, Paris
pairs.shows: corner shopfront with full carved-and-gilded wood boiserie, painted decorative panels, and period boulangerie/patisserie signage still in place under later shop occupancy — frontal, well lit, whole facade legible
pairs.street: 21 rue de Sévigné / 23 rue des Francs-Bourgeois, 4e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Porte cochère du 26 rue de la Tombe-Issoire octobre 2021
pairs.shows: single carriage door (porte cochère), dead-frontal, full height with stone surround and arch, street furniture (wheelie bin, delivery van) beside it giving a legible scale reference for the door as the absolute-scale ruler

pairs.title: Devanture Boulangerie 159 rue Ordener
pairs.shows: full corner boulangerie shopfront, dead-frontal, dark-blue painted woodwork with gilt lettering, painted glass panels, full storefront glazing down to a panelled base — whole facade legible

pairs.title: Devanture églomisée 20050917 — Boulangerie, rue de la Roquette corner
pairs.shows: corner boulangerie, dead-frontal, green marble-clad base, gilt raised lettering signboard, awning, full storefront glazing — clean full-facade shot
pairs.street: corner of rue de la Roquette, Paris

pairs.title: Devanture de la maison Hébrard, 8 rue Royale, 8ème arrondissement, Paris (PH23412)
pairs.shows: period photograph of a luxury foundry/gallery shopfront on rue Royale with a sculpted stone lintel relief (Bourdelle) over full-height glazed shop windows and applied bronze lettering — dead-frontal, whole facade legible

pairs.title: Comptoir Général de Brosserie, 6 rue de Vaucouleurs, Paris
pairs.shows: plain painted timber shopfront with hand-painted signage and a folding steel security grille pulled across the glazing — good example of a modest, unrestored shopfront with its original ironwork shutter

pairs.title: Detail of the facade of an old bakery at Emilio-Castelar street and Charenton street in Paris
pairs.shows: corner boulangerie shopfront ("Boulangerie Viennoise"), dead-frontal, dark marbled base, painted glass corner panels, full storefront glazing and cafe-style outdoor tables — whole facade legible
pairs.street: corner of rue Emilio-Castelar and rue de Charenton, 12e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Paris 75010 Passage du Marché - 2016-01-09
pairs.shows: row of two adjoining ground-floor shopfronts on a narrow passage — one an ornate red-and-gold "Confiseur" boutique, one a plain grilled/shuttered unit — dead-frontal, good comparison of shopfront finish levels side by side

pairs.title: Portail d'entrée du Castel Béranger (Hector Guimard)
pairs.shows: Guimard whiplash wrought-iron entrance gate (copper + blue-green iron) with sculpted stone surround -- the canonical Art Nouveau ironwork reference

pairs.title: Édicule Guimard, Metro Porte Dauphine canopy
pairs.shows: Guimard's cast-iron whiplash canopy structure with amber glass panels -- the definitive Art Nouveau ironwork motif in built form
pairs.street: Place du Maréchal-de-Lattre-de-Tassigny (Porte Dauphine), 16e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Hôtel Mezzara (Hector Guimard)
pairs.shows: Frontal townhouse facade with a full-height projecting central bay carried up past the cornice into a curved gable, plus a whiplash wrought-iron balcony rail

pairs.title: 26 rue Vavin (Henri Sauvage)
pairs.shows: The canonical Sauvage rue Vavin stepped ('à gradins') facade in white ceramic tile, terraces set back above the lower floors -- clean frontal view

pairs.title: Immeuble d'angle, 1 rue Boulard
pairs.shows: Corner Art Nouveau apartment building (architect Léon Boucher) with continuous stacked curved balconies/oriels projecting from the facade up to and past the cornice
pairs.street: 1 rue Boulard (angle 11 rue Froidevaux), 14e arrondissement, Paris

pairs.title: Façade sur rue et square d'Orléans, 80 rue Taitbout, 9ème arrondissement, Paris
pairs.shows: flat plastered street facade with pilasters, wrought-iron balcony railings, and rusticated arched carriage entrance — pre-Haussmann envelope of a grand Restauration-era private residential enclave

pairs.title: Vue de la cour, square d'Orléans, 9ème arrondissement, Paris
pairs.shows: colonnaded courtyard facade with Ionic columns and continuous wrought-iron balcony rail — grand Restauration/Louis-Philippe classical detailing

pairs.title: Immeuble, 84 rue de la Victoire, 9ème arrondissement, Paris
pairs.shows: full street row of flat plastered facades with continuous thin wrought-iron balcony railings and shuttered windows above period shopfronts

pairs.title: Immeuble, 87 rue de la Victoire, 9ème arrondissement, Paris
pairs.shows: row of flat plastered facades with shuttered windows, thin iron balcony railings, and carved frieze band above ground-floor shops

pairs.title: 13 rue de la Tour-des-Dames, Paris 9e
pairs.shows: close frontal detail of plain plastered facade with thin scrolled/lozenge wrought-iron balcony railings — direct evidence for the family's ironwork motif

pairs.title: Cité Malesherbes, Paris 9e 2-1
pairs.shows: flat plastered facade with decorative panel reliefs and thin scrolled wrought-iron balcony railings above the gated entrance to a Louis-Philippe-era artists' cité
pairs.street: Cité Malesherbes, accès 59 rue des Martyrs, Paris 9e

pairs.title: 1-3 Place Saint-Michel
pairs.shows: Corner block: 45-degree mansard comble with round dormers, bossage-rusticated ground-floor arcades, continuous balcon filant with sculpted balustrade at 2nd floor and plain ironwork balcon filant at top (5th/6th) floor, strict cornice-line unity across the block.

pairs.title: 1-7 Place Saint-Michel
pairs.shows: Two adjacent Second Empire buildings sharing identical cornice, mansard-roof, and balcon-filant lines across the parcel boundary -- clean evidence of strict block unity.

pairs.title: Avenue de l'Opéra no. 38
pairs.shows: Near-frontal full facade: sculpted balcon filant with scrollwork balustrade at 2nd floor, plainer continuous balcon filant at top floor just under the comble, dormers with round pediments, giving a clean read of the two-balcon-band rule.

pairs.title: 50 Boulevard Magenta, caryatid detail
pairs.shows: Close detail of a sculpted caryatid (by Charles Gauthier) supporting the 2nd-floor balcon filant, with the wrought-iron balustrade of the floor above visible -- clean evidence of the ornamental treatment at the balcon-filant floor.

pairs.title: 56 Boulevard Magenta, atlas figures
pairs.shows: Close detail of paired sculpted atlas figures (by Sébastien Delarue) framing a window below a continuous ironwork balcon filant -- dated facade (1866-1867), squarely inside the canonical Second Empire window.

pairs.title: Boulevard de Sébastopol corner
pairs.shows: Corner building on one of Haussmann's first pierced boulevards: mansard comble, continuous balcon filant at 2nd floor and dormer-level balustrade at top floor, ground-floor shopfronts under a rusticated base.

pairs.title: Haussmannian building with corner dome
pairs.shows: Corner pavilion with a domed roof and a row of near-identical Haussmannian buildings receding down the block, each with matching balcon-filant bands -- good block-unity evidence, oblique/receding framing.
pairs.street: Paris (exact address not recorded on Commons)

pairs.title: 105 & 107 Rue de Rennes
pairs.shows: Near-frontal facade with full-height sculpted caryatids flanking the ground-floor shopfronts, a decorated balcon filant at 2nd floor immediately above them, and a plainer continuous balcon filant at the top floor below the comble.

pairs.title: Rue Halévy dormers and comble detail
pairs.shows: Close, upward-angled detail of the mansard comble: a run of pedimented dormer windows above a continuous wrought-iron balcon filant and Corinthian-capped pilasters -- clean evidence of the roof/comble geometry and top-floor balcony band.

pairs.title: 12 Rue Halévy
pairs.shows: Full, near-frontal corner facade: rusticated bossage ground floor with round-arched openings, continuous balcon filant at 2nd floor, plain ironwork balcon filant at top floor just under the mansard comble -- one of the cleanest single-image reads of the whole family's defining stack.

pairs.title: 16 rue Etienne-Marcel
pairs.shows: whole facade: mascaron heads under balcony console brackets, richly molded window surrounds with alternating pediments, wrought-iron balconies -- textbook Third Republic ornament density

pairs.title: 53 rue Blanche
pairs.shows: whole facade, frontal: carved sculpted keystones/roundels above two window bands and an arched porte-cochere with carved surround -- 45-degree-comble roofline visible above

pairs.title: Immeuble haussmannien (corner facade detail)
pairs.shows: close, mildly oblique crop of a corner facade: repeated carved lintel roundels above windows, dense wrought-iron balcony rows across two floor bands

pairs.title: 105 rue de Rennes, caryatids flanking window
pairs.shows: frontal detail: full-figure sculpted caryatids flanking a piano-nobile window in place of a plain console -- an extreme, dated example of window treatment becoming sculptural rather than just corniced

pairs.title: 107 rue de Rennes, caryatids flanking window
pairs.shows: frontal detail, the neighbouring building's matching pair of sculpted caryatids at a window -- same treatment as 105 rue de Rennes, confirms it as a deliberate facade-wide scheme rather than a one-off

pairs.title: 1 bis place de l'Alma, mascaron over porte-cochere
pairs.shows: sharp frontal close-up of a smiling female mascaron set in a foliate surround above a wrought-iron porte-cochere -- clean example of mascaron-as-standard-ornament over an entrance

pairs.title: 14 boulevard Saint-Michel, window pediment with mascaron
pairs.shows: sharp frontal close-up of a broken-scroll window pediment with a mascaron head at the centre flanked by fruit swags -- textbook combination of the richening pediment and the mascaron becoming standard vocabulary

pairs.title: Mascaron detail, Paris
pairs.shows: very sharp frontal close-up of a bearded male mascaron keystone -- good clean reference for carving style even though the source building/address is not recorded

pairs.title: 47 rue du Faubourg Montmartre, mascaron keystone over door
pairs.shows: sharp frontal close-up of a bearded mascaron keystone over a carved segmental-arch door pediment with fruit swags -- another clean pediment+mascaron pairing

pairs.title: Paris zinc roofs with dormers and chimney stacks
pairs.shows: close-up of zinc standing-seam (tasseaux) roofing texture on a straight comble, two box dormers with white sashes, souches (chimney stacks) with multiple flues and cowls, a roof hatch and a tabatiere (slope skylight)

pairs.title: Mansard roof with pedimented dormers, Paris
pairs.shows: textbook comble a la Mansart profile: slate brisis (steep lower slope) meeting a near-flat zinc terrasson at the ridge, four evenly spaced pedimented (triangular-fronton) dormers each with a small cast-iron balustrade, souche at right, cornice with anthemion antefixes below

pairs.title: Rue d'Alger roofline and balcony
pairs.shows: straight 45-degree zinc comble with three box dormers directly above a continuous balcon filant (top-floor running balcony) with a geometric cast-iron railing, persiennes (louvered shutters) on the floor below, souche at center

pairs.title: Haussmannian roofline, Rue Halevy
pairs.shows: low-angle view of a cornice line with six evenly spaced pedimented dormers on a straight comble, a balcon filant with dense symmetrical cast-iron scrollwork at the floor below the cornice, foliated console brackets over the windows

pairs.title: Haussmannian immeuble roofline
pairs.shows: roofline continuity across two adjoining party-wall buildings: straight slate/zinc combles with box (lucarne rentrante) dormers, continuous cornice, souches with terracotta chimney pots, and a top-floor balcony with cast-iron railing at the corner

pairs.title: 53 Rue Blanche facade
pairs.shows: complete canonical elevation: ashlar (pierre de taille) facade with carriage-door arch, a balcon filant at the 2nd floor and a second balcon filant at the 5th (top) floor exactly as the family brief describes, straight zinc comble with box dormers and souches above

pairs.title: Roofscape from Boulevard Malesherbes
pairs.shows: elevated quarter view of straight 45-degree combles lining up across a block, row of oval-topped dormers along one ridge, souches punctuating the skyline, balcon filant band on the facade below, Eiffel Tower on the horizon for scale/orientation

pairs.title: Chimney stacks over Paris roofs
pairs.shows: dense field of souches (party-wall chimney stacks) each capped with multiple terracotta chimney pots, stepping back across successive roof ridges; straight zinc combles visible lower right and center

pairs.title: Rooftops of Rue Danielle Casanova
pairs.shows: straight zinc comble with three small hipped/pyramidal-roofed dormers (chien-assis type, plainer than a pedimented lucarne) sitting directly above a balcon filant with simple iron railings, souches with terracotta pots on the flanking party walls

pairs.title: Boulevard de Sebastopol
pairs.shows: unbroken cornice/balcony line running at consistent height across a long row of separate buildings down Boulevard de Sebastopol — the clearest single piece of evidence in this set for the 1855 circulaire's block-alignment requirement; straight 45-degree mansard roofs throughout, no curved combles or corner domes

pairs.title: Cornice and Dormers, Rue Halevy
pairs.shows: tight, well-lit crop of the main roof cornice with closely spaced block modillions and dentils, straight-sided pedimented dormers set into a true 45-degree slate mansard, and a dense cast-scrollwork running balcony immediately below — the canonical Second Empire cornice profile

pairs.title: Bandeau and Cornice Detail, Rue Halevy
pairs.shows: two stacked horizontal members on the same facade in one frame: a plain corniced bandeau/string-course marking a storey division, and above it the deeper main roof cornice with sculpted console-modillions and dentils, plus a dense cast-iron scrollwork balustrade and straight pedimented dormers

pairs.title: 12 Rue Halevy Corner Elevation
pairs.shows: full corner elevation with the main cornice and two intermediate bandeaux running unbroken around the curved corner bay at identical height on both street facades, dense wrought-iron balconies at the 2nd and 5th floors, and rusticated (bossage) ground floor with round-arched openings

pairs.title: 16 Rue Berthollet Facade
pairs.shows: full ashlar facade with a plain corniced string course under the top-floor balcony and a deeper modillioned cornice with paired console brackets under the 2nd-floor balcony, pedimented window surrounds at the piano nobile, dense scrollwork balcon filant at 2nd and top floors, and the next building visible at matching cornice height to the right

pairs.title: Avenue de l'Opera Enfilade
pairs.shows: long raking view down a full block showing the roof cornice, modillion band, and running balcony continuing unbroken at identical height across many distinct building facades receding into the distance — the single most legible illustration of the 1855 circulaire's mandated horizontal continuity across party walls in this set, though the exact construction date of this stretch of the avenue (built in stages 1864-1879) could not be confirmed as pre-1870

pairs.title: Typical Haussmannian Facade
pairs.shows: full elevation with a block-modillioned main cornice under a straight 45-degree slate mansard, a plain bandeau string course marking the 2nd-floor division, dense cast-iron balcon filant, and flat ashlar wall plane with minimal relief; a second, differently detailed building is visible immediately adjoining at left for comparison

pairs.title: Hôtel privé, 8 rue de Valois-du-Roule — élévation principale
pairs.shows: Full principal elevation, 'Hôtel privé, Première Classe': straight 45° mansard comble with pedimented dormers and cresting, running wrought-iron balconies at two floors, rusticated ground floor, flat wall plane in pierre de taille, printed metric scale bar for direct measurement.

pairs.title: Hôtel privé, 8 rue de Turin — croisées du rez-de-chaussée (détail mesuré)
pairs.shows: Large-scale measured detail of a ground-floor window bay with full dimension callouts in metres: bossage coursing on the socle, wrought-iron balcon-garde-corps scrollwork, entablature and pediment mouldings — a plate answerable to exact proportions rather than a photograph's estimate.

pairs.title: Hôtel privé, 17 rue Vanneau — élévation principale
pairs.shows: Textbook narrow street-front elevation, 'Deuxième Classe': straight comble with three pedimented dormers, continuous cast-iron balconies at two floors, flat unadorned ashlar wall plane, ground-floor door and barred windows — the canonical narrow haussmannien house front with printed metric scale.

pairs.title: Hôtel privé, 17 rue Vanneau — élévation postérieure (façade sur cour)
pairs.shows: Companion rear/courtyard elevation of the same house: plainer treatment than the street front, still with balconies and a straight comble at every floor, showing how the classical street facade contrasts with the working courtyard face of an identical structure.

pairs.title: Maison à loyer, avenue de l'Impératrice — coupe générale
pairs.shows: Full building section ('coupe générale') cut through the porte-cochère passage: interior room heights and decor at left against the exterior street elevation at right, courtyard, and rear service wing — the single plate type in this family that reveals true floor-to-floor heights rather than only the outward face.
pairs.street: avenue de l'Impératrice (today avenue Foch), Paris

pairs.title: Maison à loyer, 3 rue de la Paix — élévation
pairs.shows: A 'Première Classe' rental building (the standard haussmannien maison à loyer type): ground-floor shopfronts, two full-width running iron balconies (2nd and 5th-floor pattern), straight mansard comble with pedimented dormers, and a flat symmetrical facade plane — the clearest single-plate demonstration of the balcon filant rule.

pairs.title: Maison à loyer, 120 boulevard de Sébastopol — détails de la façade
pairs.shows: Fully measured entrance-bay detail on the flagship percée boulevard: entresol window and door surround with dimensioned mouldings, balcony-console profile with metric callouts, door hardware — usable for exact proportions of the rez-de-chaussée treatment that a photograph could not supply.

pairs.title: Maison à loyer, 9 rue du Conservatoire — détail de la façade
pairs.shows: Two stacked measured window bays with cast-iron balcon-filant railings, floral rosette bandeau, and dimensioned mouldings/reveals in metres and centimetres — a second independent source for exact balcony and window proportions.

pairs.title: Maison à loyer, 63 boulevard de Sébastopol — détail de la façade
pairs.shows: Measured door/window-pediment detail with a full dimension ladder in the margin: cartouche carving, bossage coursing either side of the opening, and an arched porte-cochère lintel below — another exact-proportions source for ground-floor surrounds on the same boulevard.

pairs.title: Immeuble rue Halévy -- élévation type du décret de 1860
pairs.shows: Round-arched pedestrian entrance with a single mascaron keystone set directly beside a full cast-iron-framed shopfront (now Zara) at the same ground-floor datum, with the complete balcon-filant / pedimented-dormer comble stack above -- Commons' own title calls this the model elevation prescribed by the 1860 decree.

pairs.title: Le Grand Hôtel, boulevard des Capucines
pairs.shows: The Grand Hôtel's arcaded former main entrance and flanking shop bays, each round arch fitted with a dense wrought-iron scrolled grille, directly beside contemporary shopfronts at street level -- Commons dates the Jules Cavelier atlantes on the facade above the arcade to 'vers 1861/1862', an independently sourced construction date rather than a photo-capture date.

pairs.title: 27, rue Saint-Lazare
pairs.shows: A paired entrance bay: a full carriage-height round-arched porte cochère (iron gate visible through the opening) beside a matching pedestrian door, both set under an ornamented cast-iron fanlight grille with a carved cartouche between them -- an unusually clean read of a genuine two-door Second Empire entrance and its ironwork.

pairs.title: 2, place d'Estienne d'Orves
pairs.shows: A deep-red double-leaf porte cochère flanked by carved telamon figures, standing directly beside a café-brasserie awning on one side and a bank shopfront on the other -- a strong side-by-side contrast between the entrance's height and the shopfronts' more modest scale on the same ground floor.
pairs.street: 2 place d'Estienne d'Orves / 60 rue de Châteaudun, Paris 9e

pairs.title: 2, boulevard Voltaire
pairs.shows: A plain, unornamented wood double-leaf porte cochère beside a rolled-steel shop shutter and a restaurant awning -- the one 'ordinary register' entrance kept in the set, a counterweight to the grand corner buildings that otherwise dominate what Commons has catalogued for this feature.

pairs.title: 53, rue Blanche
pairs.shows: A tall arched pale-green painted wood porte cochère with a plain moulded surround, directly beside a real-estate-agency shopfront -- full facade above shows the plain window surrounds, small pediments and continuous wrought-iron balconies of a restrained mid-register building; also used in the se-comble family for its roofline.

pairs.title: Boulevard Malesherbes, du Boulevard de Courcelles
pairs.shows: Genuine period photograph (Commons dates it ca.1853-70, taken by the City of Paris's official photographer during construction of the boulevard itself). Near-frontal view of the corner block: unbroken cornice line across party walls, continuous balcon filant at 2nd floor running the full block, straight-pitch mansard with regular dormers, flat unbroken wall plane -- the textbook block-unity effect the 1855 circulaire was written to produce.

pairs.title: Boulevard Sebastopol
pairs.shows: Genuine period photograph, corner building pavement-to-ridge in near-frontal view: straight 45-degree comble roof with segmental-pedimented dormers, continuous balcon filant at 2nd floor across the whole block, ground-floor shopfronts under a classical pilastered corner surround ('Pygmalion' sign). One of the cleanest period-authentic references for the roof/balcony/cornice relationship.

pairs.title: Rue de Turbigo
pairs.shows: Genuine period photograph of the corner building on rue de Turbigo (pierced 1854-1868), near-frontal, full height visible: ground-floor shopfronts, fenestration rhythm and pilaster articulation across 4-5 storeys, balconies at multiple levels, mansard partially visible at top. A sculpted corner figure is a single accent piece, not the near-universal caryatid escalation of the 1880s-90s.

pairs.title: Boulevard de Sebastopol (modern)
pairs.shows: Modern mild-oblique photo of a corner immeuble on boulevard de Sebastopol (pierced 1855-58): full elevation pavement-to-ridge, straight comble, two levels of continuous balcon filant, corner chamfer. Direct present-day counterpart to the Marville photographs of the same street.

pairs.title: 2 boulevard Voltaire
pairs.shows: Dead-frontal, textbook canonical elevation: straight 45-degree comble with regularly spaced pedimented dormers, continuous balcon filant at both the 2nd floor and the top floor, flat unornamented wall plane, symmetrical window bays. Ground-floor bossage is partly masked by a shop awning but the storey stack and roof are fully legible -- probably the single best reference image in this set for the cornice-to-comble relationship.

pairs.title: 53 rue Blanche
pairs.shows: Dead-frontal full elevation, pavement to ridge: straight-pitch mansard with regular dormers, arched carriage-entry door with keystone on axis, individual balconies at most floors plus continuous filant bands at two levels, flat minimal-relief wall plane. One of the clearest single-building references in the set for the overall storey stack.

pairs.title: 3 place Saint-Michel, balcon, toit
pairs.shows: Tight upward-angled crop of the corner mansard and the floor just below it: a dense, symmetrical cast-iron balcon-filant balustrade (fine interlocking scrollwork, no whiplash asymmetry) running along the whole visible bay, plus small matching wrought-iron balconettes on the dormer windows in the zinc comble itself. A rule about the standard haussmannien scrollwork pattern, or about ironwork repeating at the attic-storey dormers, is directly answerable to this image.

pairs.title: 23, avenue de l'Opéra (1916)
pairs.shows: Long raking street view down the full enfilade: a continuous balcon filant carried across ten-plus separate party-wall bays at a consistent floor line, exactly the block-wide horizontal continuity the 1855 circulaire was written to force. Photograph itself dates to 1916 (irrelevant photo-capture date, not used as a construction date) but the ironwork and stone are photographed close enough to their construction to be undisturbed by later renovation.

pairs.title: Boulevard de Sébastopol, street elevation
pairs.shows: Clear daylight street view with buildings on both sides showing matching balcon-filant bands at consistent floor heights running the length of the visible block. Boulevard de Sébastopol was pierced 1855-1858, among the very first Second Empire percées, so this street is safely inside the 1853-1870 window.

pairs.title: Corner building dated 1858, boulevard de Sébastopol
pairs.shows: Upward corner view with dense, rich cast-iron scrollwork balconies at two consecutive floors, foliage partly overhanging the top-left corner but the ironwork itself fully legible. A construction date, '1858', is cut directly into the stone pier at the corner and clearly visible in the photograph (not a Commons photo-capture date) -- a rare case in this corpus of an on-facade date within the strict 1853-1870 window.
pairs.street: boulevard de Sébastopol, Paris (exact house number not recorded on Commons)

pairs.title: Fontaine Saint-Michel and adjoining block
pairs.shows: Wide panorama of the whole place: on the right, an unbroken run of matching balcon filant and matching 45-degree combles across the full block from the corner around to the side street, visibly the same design repeated building to building -- the clearest 'enforced block unity' composition in this set, even though individual railing patterns read smaller than in the tight crops.

pairs.title: Immeuble, rue Halévy
pairs.shows: Full, near-frontal facade in even light: two bands of dense symmetrical cast-iron balcon filant (2nd floor and 5th floor under the straight comble), Corinthian-pilaster window surrounds, a mascaron keystone over the ground-floor arch, and pedimented dormers. A clean, unobstructed reference for how the two balcony bands sit relative to the whole elevation.

pairs.title: Rue Halévy, dormer and balustrade detail
pairs.shows: Tight upward crop pairing two pedimented dormers on a straight comble with the dense cast-iron balustrade of the balcon filant directly below -- a good answerable image for how the roofline dormer rhythm and the ironwork band relate vertically on the same facade.

pairs.title: Boulevard de Sébastopol, sidewalk enfilade
pairs.shows: Street-level view down a long stretch of sidewalk: a continuous line of cast-iron balconies at matching floor heights recurs down the whole visible block on the right, receding into the distance -- direct visual evidence of the 1855 circulaire's block-wide alignment rule holding over many buildings, not just two.

pairs.title: 3 Boulevard Malesherbes, ground-floor arcade
pairs.shows: Four arched ground-floor bays with regular raised bossage: each pier and voussoir band is built from cleanly coursed ashlar blocks with deep, evenly-spaced horizontal and radiating joints -- the coursing module is constant across all four bays, giving a clean real-world course-height figure. Boulevard Malesherbes was pierced 1861-1870, squarely inside the target period. Cropped to exclude the tour bus that partly blocked the original frame.

pairs.title: 84 Boulevard Malesherbes, porte-cochère surround
pairs.shows: Ground-floor socle in regular coursed ashlar with drafted-margin joints framing the arched porte-cochère and flanking windows -- clean, unbroken horizontal coursing from the pavement to the first-floor cornice, giving a legible course-height dimension. Parked cars intrude only at the very bottom of frame.

pairs.title: 86 Boulevard Malesherbes, porte-cochère surround
pairs.shows: Same coursed-ashlar socle module as its neighbours at 84 and 88 -- useful as a repeat confirming the course height is a fixed design dimension along this stretch of the boulevard, not a one-off. Tree shadow falls across the stone but does not obscure the joint lines.

pairs.title: 88 Boulevard Malesherbes, porte-cochère surround
pairs.shows: Third repeat of the same coursed-ashlar ground-floor socle module seen at 84 and 86 Boulevard Malesherbes -- door surround and window jambs built from regular drafted-margin blocks, clean and well lit, minimal obstruction.

pairs.title: 62 rue de Malte, door and entresol
pairs.shows: French Wikipedia's own bossage article captions this exact photo as an example of 'bossage a refend continu en tables' -- the flat-panelled, continuously-jointed variant of bossage, visible here as the shallow horizontal banding on the pale entresol wall between the carved door surround and the window above. Sharp, unobstructed, full vertical bay in frame. Note this is the flatter table-bossage variant, not deep cushioned rustication -- record it as such rather than over-claiming.

pairs.title: 16 Avenue Victoria, dated pilaster panel
pairs.shows: Ground-floor pilaster panel between two shopfronts, carved with 'A. HUGUET ARCHITECTE 1860' directly on the stone -- a rare case where the construction year is stated on the building itself rather than inferred. Flat recessed-panel treatment (refend-style) rather than raised bossage, bordered by grooved reveals; shop signage crops in at both edges but the dated panel itself is fully legible.

pairs.title: 133 Boulevard Haussmann, dated porte-cochère
pairs.shows: Porte-cochère lintel carved 'MONGE ARCH[itec]te 1868' plus the house number 133 -- another on-stone dated example, squarely in the target window. Flanking pilasters show flat sunken ashlar panels (refend treatment) rather than deep bossage; included for the secure date and clean coursing rather than as a bossage exemplar.

pairs.title: 34 rue Jean-Baptiste-Pigalle, window detail 05
pairs.shows: Moulded architrave and plain cornice over a window with simple balcon filant ironwork below -- the canonical restrained Second Empire surround with no mascaron.

pairs.title: 34 rue Jean-Baptiste-Pigalle, window detail 06
pairs.shows: An upper-floor window with a small triangular fronton and a modest acanthus-and-rosette relief in the tympanum, plain shutters, no balcony -- direct evidence of ornament diminishing on higher floors versus the piano-nobile treatment.

pairs.title: Balcon d'un immeuble parisien
pairs.shows: Full window opening: triangular pediment with a shell cartouche in the tympanum on console brackets, dentilled cornice, moulded architrave, and a dense cast-iron balcon filant with heart/quatrefoil scrollwork below -- a textbook console-and-fronton-over-balcon assembly.

pairs.title: 31 rue Du Sommerard
pairs.shows: Whole corner facade showing the diminution rule end to end: pedimented 2nd-floor windows over a balustraded balcon filant, plainer moulded surrounds at 3rd floor, simple surrounds above, bossage/rustication at the arcaded ground floor shopfront, and a straight 45-degree comble with pedimented dormers on top.

pairs.title: 53 rue Blanche
pairs.shows: Full flat-plane facade across five floors: small plain rosette medallions (not full mascaron faces) at the spandrels of the two main floors, continuous cast-iron balconies at multiple levels, and visibly plainer top-floor windows -- ornament kept sparing and diminishing rather than dense.

pairs.title: 50-52 rue Notre-Dame-de-Lorette, window detail
pairs.shows: Complete window opening in one frame: triangular pediment on console brackets, egg-and-dart and dentil moulding, full architrave with sill/appui, cast-iron balcon filant below the sash, and a plainer shuttered window above it showing the upper-floor diminution. Kept for how completely it frames the opening even though the building's exact construction date could not be confirmed (klass left unknown).

pairs.title: Paris windows and dormer windows, haussmannian facade
pairs.shows: Straight 45-degree comble with plain rectangular dormers above a balcon filant, and below it Corinthian-capital console brackets crowning plain window surrounds -- the roofline-to-window relationship the diminution rule depends on.

pairs.title: Rue Halevy, 12
pairs.shows: Whole corner block facade near the Opera quarter: straight mansard roofline, arcaded rusticated ground floor with voussoired arches, continuous balcon filant at two levels, pilastered piano nobile, and consistent floor-to-floor treatment continuing across the party wall to the left -- good context shot for how the window-surround programme sits inside the whole elevation.

pairs.title: Rue Halevy 069
pairs.shows: Close view straight up the facade: two dormers with plain straight triangular pediments (not curved -- the pre-1884 comble type) sitting above a dense cast-iron balcon filant with rosette/heart motifs and a modillion cornice.

pairs.title: 19 rue Auber
pairs.shows: Two windows with matching triangular frontons on console brackets and a palmette-frieze architrave over a shared balcon filant, plus a single restrained male-mask keystone over the arched ground-floor entry below -- shows mascarons used sparingly (one, at the door) rather than on every opening.

pairs.title: 164 rue du Faubourg-Saint-Honore
pairs.shows: Multi-floor facade with cartouche-topped pediments and a full balustrade balcon filant at the 2nd floor, a simpler cartouche treatment at the 3rd, and plain surrounds with small console brackets at the 4th -- a clean four-floor progression of diminishing ornament over a scrolled-console entry arch.
